original_question: Improve the current lower and upper bounds on the number of non-isomorphic visibility graphs of simple polygons with n vertices.
target_in_paper: Section 4.8, Open Problem 40 (“Counting Visibility Graphs”): improve the lower and upper bounds on the number of non-isomorphic visibility graphs of simple polygons. The surrounding sentence specializes this to simple polygons with n vertices and gives the benchmark bounds discussed there. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target: it asks for sharper lower and upper bounds, it is about non-isomorphic visibility graphs, and it keeps the scope to simple polygons with n vertices, which is exactly the subject of Section 4.8, Open Problem 40. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
missing_details: The paper is counting vertex visibility graphs G(P) of simple polygons P; this should be stated explicitly, because the survey also studies visibility graphs of point sets and segment sets in other sections. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

A visibility graph of a simple polygon has one graph vertex for each polygon vertex, and two such graph vertices are adjacent iff the segment joining the corresponding polygon vertices lies entirely within the polygon; under the paper’s convention, this segment may pass through a reflex vertex or graze along a polygon edge. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

The count is up to graph isomorphism, not up to labeling of polygon vertices and not up to polygon similarity. Section 4.8 explicitly defines graph isomorphism and then separately notes that isomorphic visibility graphs need not come from similar polygons. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

For a stand-alone formulation, it helps to introduce a counting function such as N(n) = the number of pairwise non-isomorphic visibility graphs of simple n-vertex polygons. This notation is not in the paper, but it is the minimal way to make the question self-contained without broadening it. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

The nearby context should be built into the question: the paper’s benchmark bounds are N(n) >= 2^(n-4) and N(n) <= 2^{O(n log n)}. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=9f88e968f29258f3f50459952ccc4e41b40a1988&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The scope should say simple polygons only (so, not polygons with holes), because the general introduction discusses polygons with or without holes, but Open Problem 40 is specifically about simple polygons. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
It is natural to state n >= 3, since the objects being counted are simple n-gons; the paper leaves this implicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

The word “current” is ambiguous in 2026; for paper-faithfulness it should mean the bounds quoted in Section 4.8 of this paper, not necessarily the best bounds known later in the literature. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

There are no ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or “for all sufficiently large n” conditions here; the hidden assumptions are geometric and graph-theoretic rather than algebraic. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
refined_question: For each integer n >= 3, let N(n) denote the number of pairwise non-isomorphic vertex visibility graphs G(P) arising from simple polygons P with n vertices, where G(P) has one vertex for each vertex of P and two vertices are adjacent exactly when the segment joining the corresponding polygon vertices lies entirely in P (with the paper’s convention that the segment may pass through a reflex vertex or graze along a polygon edge). Determine asymptotically sharper lower and upper bounds for N(n), improving on the bounds 2^(n-4) <= N(n) <= 2^{O(n log n)} quoted in Section 4.8. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
justification: This rewrite stays exactly on Open Problem 40 rather than drifting to neighboring recognition, reconstruction, or similarity problems. It adds only what the paper leaves implicit but needed for a stand-alone question: the vertex-visibility definition, the fact that the count is modulo graph isomorphism, the restriction to simple polygons, and the benchmark bounds from the surrounding context. The paragraph immediately after Open Problem 40 is also why the wording must stay in graph-isomorphism terms rather than polygon-similarity terms. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
